Think it's too late to start sowing this late in the season? Think again! Even though the growing season may be past its peak, there's still plenty to sow and grow now. In this week's episode Ben demonstrates his favorite late summer seeds to see us through the autu
items.why_watch: If you've mentally written off your garden until spring, GrowVeg makes a concrete case for seven specific crops — think garlic, winter lettuce, and broad beans — that actually benefit from a September start. The video is paced around the logic of why each seed works now, not just a list to copy. Useful whether you have a full plot or just a few containers going into the cooler months.

items.why_watch: Bernadette Banner sits down with the costume designer behind 'MADFABULOUS' to pull apart the specific decisions that make period drama clothing feel lived-in rather than costumed — fabric sourcing, aging techniques, the tension between historical accuracy and what reads on camera. It's a rare peek behind a production that most viewers only see from the front row. Even if you're not a maker yourself, the conversation reframes how you'll look at clothes on screen.

items.title: How North Sea Trawler Crews Sleep in 50 Foot Waves
items.description:
Step aboard and discover what it's really like to live, work, and survive on the open ocean—subscribe now for an inside look at life at sea! 🌊⛴️🧭

https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCPBZi4fgqeGteT1jLkA6hzQ?sub_confirmation=1

This video was produced exclusively for Life at Sea. We created this content to provide an immersive look into the realities of maritime life, uncovering the daily routines, onboard systems, and human experiences that define existence aboard vessels navigating the world's tou
items.why_watch: The central question — how do you actually sleep when your bunk is pitching through 50-foot swells — turns out to have genuinely clever, low-tech answers that the crew walks through on camera. Beyond the sleep logistics, the video builds an honest picture of what sensory and physical exhaustion looks like across a multi-day trawler shift. It's the kind of specific, unglamorous working-life documentation that's hard to find done this well.

global_silver_linings.snippet: An artist is carving out a living by making amazingly-realistic wooden sculptures—after teaching himself how to use a chainsaw. The 53-year-old started carving with chainsaws 30 years ago and now makes thousands, selling his unique commission pieces across the UK. Simon Bogg usuallly spends up to three days working eight hour shifts to craft his […] The post Self-Taught Artist Carves Logs into Amazing Sculptures Using a Chainsaw appeared first on Good News Network .
global_silver_linings.reason: A self-taught artist transforming fallen logs into chainsaw sculptures is a beautiful reminder that creativity needs no formal permission — just curiosity, patience, and a willingness to learn. It also means wood that might otherwise be discarded gets a second, stunning life.

garden_note.note: The August full moon rises with an almost theatrical confidence tonight, flooding Zürich's gardens in silver just as the dahlias and late-summer zinnias hold their last warm colours before dusk swallows them. There is a particular stillness to the garden at this hour — the air still carrying the day's warmth, the nights beginning, ever so quietly, to hint at what September has in mind.
